title: Behold the Wretch Whose Lust and Wine
description: Behold the Wretch Whose Lust and Wine in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 123, headed “The repenting prodigal, Luke 15. 13 &c”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold the wretch whose lust and wine Had wast-ed his es-tate, He begs a share a-mong the swine, To taste the husks they eat!

lines: Behold the wretch whose lust and wine
He begs a share among the swine,
To taste the husks they eat!
"I'll go, and with a mournful tongue
He said, and hasten'd to his home,
The father saw the rebel come,
He ran, and fell upon his neck,
The rebel's heart with sorrow brake
"Take off his clothes of shame and sin,"
"Dress him in garments white and clean,
"My son was dead, and lives again,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
